suggestions.quote: In its glass door, your head and chip sprite flipped at about a quarter strength (cut it if it costs the week).
suggestions.fix: Decide now and cut it. Stage the kneel as a side-on silhouette against the dark gap with your chip lit beside you. That keeps the week's long pole (the city of chips on the bus, lines 118-130) free of a reflection effect.

suggestions.quote: Outside, the city passes, and over every head in it a chip: thousands, flickering, each one changing as its person moves.
suggestions.fix: Build it as two or three drifting layers of one instanced chip sprite from the rule-device kit, with only the jogger, the sleeping boy and the lit windows animated. Do not rig thousands of separate chips.

suggestions.quote: the chai stall (the stall layers from before, plus a half-down shutter)
suggestions.fix: Reuse the stall set from line 64 and add only the shutter and the tin with the second-stall drawing. Name the new props: shutter, coin tin, fee slip. Name the reused ones: hall, chair grid (lines 26 and 85), lane wall and wicket, taped bat, apron, kettle.

suggestions.quote: The crimson chip above you, out of focus.
suggestions.fix: At line 151 the chip sits at the edge of the frame, and the last 15 s keep the right third quiet. Put you and the chip in the left two-thirds, with the chip left of your head, so nothing blurred drifts into the end-screen third.

suggestions.quote: a figure in a long dark coat with a crimson head, and no chip over him at all.
suggestions.fix: Hold the stranger on screen for at least 1 s, and place him by the kettle rather than behind steam. The second-watch plant should read when the viewer rewinds. Make the missing chip the visible tell.

suggestions.quote: a small stamped paper tag that says SUBSCRIBE. No sound.
suggestions.fix: The cost beat starts right after the midpoint swell, so keep this tag small and low-left, with no cue change at the notice board. It must not read as the reveal of the chip stirring.

suggestions.quote: Montage, under a second each: you pour tea onto your own shoe; you count change wrong; you nap on a sack of tea leaves.
suggestions.fix: Give the montage three distinct poses and a one-frame camera nudge between them, so it reads in 2.5 s. This is the only stretch with three gags and no spoken line.

keep.quote: The biggest number is the right choice.
You can't borrow someone's odds. Only their apron.
